doc.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Miles Davis in Detroit; stays at the Joneses' house
summary: Miles came to the Bluebird without a band, and Elvin played with him for six months while he stayed at Elvin's house.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: Yeah that was Miles. Cause I started playing at the Bluebird in 1951 or something. Miles used to come there the same as Charlie Parker did at the Crystal Lounge. So he came to Detroit without a band at the Bluebird. Sonny Stitt would come in, a lot of guys. Ken Kimery: Miles would stay there for months on end right?

He stayed there for almost-- He would stay for months on end. I played with him for 6 months when I was playing with him. He got himself together in Detroit. Cause he wasn’t in very good shape. But he got himself together.
(addressing Keiko) So Keiko you’re saying that Miles stayed at your house?
Yeah. You know when they came in town they didn’t have—they came to my house. And I said, “Okay you know…well here it is!”
Along with what Keiko is saying she used to let you host jam sessions or let musicians come by your house?
